questions.q: MatekH743, standard build: TIM8 has outputs 1–2, TIM5 has outputs 3–6. Motors are on outputs 1–4 with `MOT_PWM_TYPE = 6`. A gripper servo is assigned to output 5 (`SERVO5_FUNCTION = 28`). What happens?
options: The servo runs at 50 Hz, because the mode and rate are set separately for every output
Output 5 is disabled and arming is refused: `SERVO5_FUNCTION=28 on disabled channel`
The whole TIM5 group falls back to PWM, and motors 3 and 4 are left without DShot
The servo gets DShot frames, with no warnings in Messages
questions.explain: The protocol is set per timer. DShot on outputs 3 and 4 switches the whole of TIM5 to digital mode; the firmware disables the other outputs of the group (`get_disabled_channels`), and the pre-arm check fails for ordinary functions (AP_Arming.cpp, `servo_checks`).

questions.q: Motors on plain PWM (`MOT_PWM_TYPE = 0`, `RC_SPEED = 490`) and an analog servo are in the same timer group of the main processor. `SERVO_RATE = 50`. What rate does the servo get?
options: 50 Hz: `SERVO_RATE` applies to every output with a servo function
490 Hz: exactly the `RC_SPEED` value
400 Hz, with no warnings
The servo output is disabled and arming is refused
questions.explain: `set_freq` applies the motor rate to the whole group and limits it to 400 Hz; `set_default_rate` skips the "fast" groups. There is no pre-arm failure: that exists only for groups with DShot and a strip. An analog servo at 400 Hz overheats.

questions.q: An output with an "angle" function (full travel 4500): `SERVOn_MIN = 1000`, `SERVOn_MAX = 2000`, `SERVOn_TRIM = 1400`, `REVERSED = 0`. The input is +3000. What pulse does the firmware output?
questions.explain: For a positive input: TRIM + ⌊s · (MAX − TRIM) / 4500⌋ = 1400 + ⌊3000 · 600 / 4500⌋ = 1400 + 400 = 1800. You get 1733 if you take half of the full span (500) instead of MAX − TRIM, and 1833 if you count from 1500.

questions.q: An octocopter on a build with bidirectional DShot: you need RPM from the motors on outputs 5–8. Which `SERVO_BLH_BDMASK` value enables exactly those?
questions.explain: Bit 0 is output 1, and the weight of output n is 2^(n − 1): 16 + 32 + 64 + 128 = 240. 480 is the mistake with the weight 2^n; 15 is outputs 1–4.

questions.q: A parameter fragment (a training example). The flight controller does not arm. Which message does the firmware give, and what do you fix?
options: `RELAY1_PIN=54, set SERVO5_FUNCTION=-1`: switch output 5 to GPIO and reboot
`RELAY1_PIN=54 invalid`: pin 54 does not exist, you need 105
`pin conflict RELAY1_PIN = RELAY2_PIN`: set `RELAY2_PIN = -1`
`Hardware safety switch`: press the safety switch
questions.explain: Pin 54 belongs to output 5 (on boards numbered from 50), and it is not a GPIO. The `AP_Relay::arming_checks` check finds the output from the pin number and names the parameter. The `invalid` message appears when the board has no pin with that number at all.

questions.q: `MOT_PWM_TYPE = 6`, `SERVO_BLH_RVMASK = 5`, `SERVO_DSHOT_ESC = 0`. Motors 1 and 3 keep spinning the same way. Why?
options: Mask 5 means outputs 5 and 1, not 1 and 3
With ESC type 0, DShot commands are not sent
Reversal works only together with `SERVO_BLH_3DMASK`
The reverse command is sent only after arming
questions.explain: `update_channel_masks` sends the reverse and 3D commands only for ESC types 1–4 and only while disarmed. Mask 5 = 4 + 1 is exactly outputs 1 and 3.

questions.q: An ESC on bidirectional DShot reports E = 1260 (in units of 100 eRPM), `SERVO_BLH_POLES = 12`. What RPM does the firmware write to the `RPM` field of the `ESC` message?
questions.explain: RPM = ⌊E · 200 / poles⌋ = 1260 · 200 / 12 = 21000. You divide by the number of pole pairs (6), not by the number of poles: 10500 is that mistake. You get 18000 with 14 poles.

questions.q: What does the `@SYS/timers.txt` file, downloaded from the flight controller over MAVFTP, contain?
options: A list of outputs with their assigned `SERVOn_FUNCTION`
One line per timer: clock frequency, mode, actual and target rate
The "pad, timer, GPIO pin number" table from the `hwdef`
Bidirectional DShot error counters for every motor
questions.explain: `RCOutput::timer_info` prints the `TIMERV1` header and lines with the fields `CLK`, `MODE`, `FREQ`, `TGT`. There are no output numbers in it; you match them to timers through `hwdef.dat`, and the `RCOut:` banner shows the mode per output.

questions.q: A board with an IOMCU, ESCs connected to MAIN 1–4, `SERVO_BLH_AUTO = 1`, the vehicle disarmed. The ESC configuration program does not find the ESCs through passthrough. What is the main cause?
options: IOMCU outputs do not work as a bridge to the ESCs, so the ESCs have to be moved to AUX
Passthrough on MAIN requires `BRD_IO_DSHOT = 1` and a reboot with the new coprocessor firmware
You need to set `SERVO_BLH_PORT = 8`
Passthrough works only while armed
questions.explain: `serial_setup_output` looks for the output only among the main processor's timer groups; outputs 1–8 on a board with an IOMCU are not in them. `BRD_IO_DSHOT` gives DShot on MAIN, but not passthrough. While armed, the handler in fact drops the requests.

questions.q: `RELAY1_FUNCTION = 1`, `RC8_OPTION = 28`, channel 8 is a three-position switch. In which position is the relay on?
options: In the middle and high positions
Only in the low position
Only in the high position
In any position except the middle
questions.explain: In `RC_Channel.cpp` the relay gets the state `ch_flag == HIGH`: it is on only in the high position, and the middle and low positions turn it off.
